newsitem.title: CANADA: SASKATCHEWAN AG SAYS HARVEST OF SPRING CROP BEGINS.
newsitem.headline: SASKATCHEWAN AG SAYS HARVEST OF SPRING CROP BEGINS.

text.p: One percent of spring-seeded crops were combined with harvest activity mainly concentrated in the southwest, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its report.
One percent of spring wheat, durum, spring rye and canola were combined by Sunday. Nine percent of field peas and eight percent of lentils were combined.
Harvest operations were one week ahead of average. Hot weather in the past week resulted in rapid crop development.
Cooler weather on the weekend brought much needed relief to heat-stressed crops. Light, scattered rains fell but were not likely to have much impact on the dried crops.
Drought stress was reported across the grainbelt. Hail damage was reported on the eastern side of the grainbelt.

The southern grainbelt saw hot and windy weather with an average 18 mm (0.8 inch) of rain. High temperatures and lack of rain caused drought stress across the region. Heavy winds scattered lentil swaths and lodged standing crops. Hail damage was reported in the southeast.
Central Saskatchewan saw dry and hot weather with no rain except in the west-central region which saw an average 27 mm (1 inch) of rain. Heat and drought stress were reported across the region.

Northern grainbelt crops saw hot and dry weather with an average 17 mm (0.8 inch) of rain. Drought and heat stress damaged crops across the region. Localized hail damage was reported in the northeast and winds caused crop damage in the northwest.
